test_title: RRB NTPC - Graduate 2025 (CBT 2) Foundational Full Test - 06
subject: general
question: Train ‘A’ requires 15 seconds to cross train ‘B’ of length 300 m moving in the opposite direction at a speed of 36 km/h. Further, train ‘A’ requires 30 seconds to cross a 500 m long stationary train ‘C’. Find the length (in m) of train ‘A’.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed of train B = 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s.

For Train A to cross Train B, relative speed = Speed to cross stationary C + Speed of B.

⇒ (LA + 300) ÷ 15 = (LA + 500) ÷ 30 + 10

⇒ 2LA + 600 = LA + 500 + 300

⇒ LA = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of train B = 300 m

Speed of train B = 36 km/h = 36 × (5/18) = 10 m/s

Length of stationary train C = 500 m

Time to cross B = 15 s, Time to cross C = 30 s

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

When moving in opposite directions, Relative Speed = VA + VB

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/769276248a78aa7449ab538025ee5c0e35cc38fac6df147a92bbfaa750d86c87.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the length of train A be LA and its speed be VA.

⇒ Time taken to cross train B = (LA + 300) ÷ (VA + 10) = 15

⇒ VA + 10 = (LA + 300) ÷ 15 --- (1)

⇒ Time taken to cross stationary train C = (LA + 500) ÷ VA = 30

⇒ VA = (LA + 500) ÷ 30 --- (2)

⇒ Substituting equation (2) into equation (1):

⇒ [(LA + 500) ÷ 30] + 10 = (LA + 300) ÷ 15

⇒ Multiplying by 30 on both sides:

⇒ LA + 500 + 300 = 2 × (LA + 300)

⇒ LA + 800 = 2LA + 600

⇒ LA = 800 − 600 = 200

**∴ The correct answer is 200 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed

For two objects moving in opposite directions, relative speed is the sum of their speeds (V₁ + V₂). For the same direction, it is the difference (V₁ − V₂).

Crossing Objects

When a train crosses an object with length (like a platform or another train), the total distance covered equals the sum of lengths (L₁ + L₂).

Speed Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5 ÷ 18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18 ÷ 5.
